subject: Re: Real-time embeddings: p50/p95 SLO ask + temporary carveout request
messages:
From: Travis Cole <tcole@astrahealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@astrahealth.com
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime embeddings SLA ask: p50/p95 and sampling during migration

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the Redwood runtime looks promising. We're preparing a production rollout of a clinical search feature that uses real-time embedding generation (per-query embeddings at the point of search). Our traffic profile is spiky (EHR-driven bursts) and we need a firm latency commitment for uptime/SLAs to proceed with the contract.

High-level ask: can Redwood commit to p50/p95 latency targets for the Hosted Embedding endpoint? Our target range is roughly p50 <= 30ms, p95 <= 120ms, measured in-region. We understand there are practicalities for embeddings (batching, KV cache, quantized model fallbacks) and we'd accept a temporary exception window while we migrate traffic and tune batching on our side.

Key constraints and asks:
- Measurement: we need p50/p95 reported daily with evidence; our compliance team requires a 24h rolling aggregation and request-level traceability (trace IDs).
- Sampling: our volume is ~120M requests/day; we'd like to discuss a sampling approach (we can provide traffic slices).
- Migration carveout: a 14-day probationary carveout during our rollout where some spikes may exceed p95; need agreed derating and rollback criteria.

I've attached a small traffic sample (traffic_sample.csv) and a short doc outlining traffic shapes. Can we get a proposed SLO framing and whether Redwood can provide a temporary exception path with clear rollback conditions?

Travis
Director, Platform Engineering
AstraHealth

Attachments: traffic_sample.csv

Hi Travis — really appreciate the context and the sample. Short answer: yes, we can work with a p50/p95 commitment for hosted embeddings, but we need to align on measurement windowing, sampling methodology, and precise carveout rules for the migration. I'll summarize an initial proposal below and will follow up with engineering for concrete telemetry checks.

Initial proposed approach (for discussion):
- Commitment: p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 150ms (in-region) for the embeddings endpoint.
- Measurement: 15-minute rolling windows, aggregated to a daily report; evidence will include request traces and sampled payloads.
- Sampling: default 0.5% per-request sampling floor, with the option to increase to 1% for your pilot days so sampling variance is small.
- Migration carveout: 14-day probationary window where deviations above p95 are tracked but do not trigger credits; rollback/review if >5% of 15-minute windows breach p95 for more than 6 hours cumulative.

Action items:
1) I'll loop in infra/telemetry to validate that the embedding endpoint exposes the per-request latency and trace IDs (cc'ing internal team).
2) Please confirm you can tag traffic slices with a header we can filter on (e.g., X-AH-Canary).
3) We'll prepare a DocuSign amendment with the probationary carveout language for signatures.

I'll circle back once I hear from Eng (ETA ~24h).

—Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding a prospective customer's request. Quick background: AstraHealth wants p50/p95 for realtime embeddings (very high QPS) and a 14-day migration carveout. They sent a small traffic sample and want daily evidence + per-request traces.

Questions we need answered for the proposal:
- Measurement granularity: is our runtime able to produce a 15-minute rolling p50/p95 for the embedding endpoint per-tenant (filtered by header) with trace ids?
- Sampling: recommend a sampling floor and variance analysis for a 120M req/day workload; is 0.5% realistic for stable p95 numbers?
- Cold-starts / quantization fallback: should we explicitly carve out first-10-minutes after deploys or quantization fallbacks? How do we detect those in telemetry?
- Billing / credits: what are safe rollback thresholds to propose (Monica's suggested >5% of windows breaching p95 for >6h cumulative)?

Attached: traffic_sample.csv (small), proposed slo-evidence-template.xlsx. Need an engineering blurb I can send to Travis.

Thanks — Monica

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Realtime embeddings SLA ask: p50/p95 and sampling during migration

Monica — quick engineering note you can paste to Travis. TL;DR: feasible with caveats.

Feasibility notes:
- Per-request telemetry: our hosted runtime emits per-request start/end timestamps, model variant, and trace id. We can filter by X-AH-Canary header to produce tenant-scoped aggregates.
- Measurement windows: recommend 15-minute rolling windows (aligned by wall-clock) aggregated to daily for SL reports. Rolling windows reduce sensitivity to minute-long spikes.
- Sampling: for 120M/day, 0.5% yields ~600k samples/day — enough for stable p95 estimates. If they want tighter confidence intervals during pilot, 1% is recommended. We'll provide estimated CI for p95 based on their sample.
- Carveouts: explicitly carve out:
  * Cold starts: first 10m after any model swap / canary switch (detect via model-variant tag in telemetry).
  * Quantization fallback: detectable via a runtime flag in traces; we can exclude those requests from SLO computation or mark them as degraded.
- Rollback thresholds: Monica's proposal (>5% of 15-min windows breach p95 for >6h cumulative in 14d window) is reasonable, but operationally we prefer a two-tier approach:
  * Tier 1 (soft): monitor and alert at 3% breach threshold.
  * Tier 2 (hard rollback): propose 7% breach threshold triggers review and potential rollback.

Action items for us:
- Instrument a temporary per-tenant SLO dashboard (15-min rolling histograms) and attach sampled traces to each violating window.
- Provide an evidence package template (I reviewed their sample; the attached slo-evidence-template.xlsx will work).

I'll prepare the CI numbers for p95 at 0.5% and 1% sampling and send by EOD.

—Karthik
Sr. Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Hi Travis — following internal review we've refined a proposal and the operational guardrails for the probationary carveout. Summary below; attaching the DocuSign proposal for signature if this matches your expectations.

Agreed proposal (summary):
- Formal SLO: p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 150ms for the Hosted Embedding endpoint (in-region).
- Measurement: 15-minute rolling windows aggregated to a daily report. SLO violations reported with attached sampled traces.
- Sampling: baseline 0.5% per-request sampling floor; AstraHealth may opt-in to 1% for pilot days. Redwood will provide estimated CI for p95 at both sampling rates.
- Carveouts:
  * 14-day probationary carveout during initial traffic migration.
  * Cold-start carveout: exclude first 10 minutes after model swaps or canary cutovers.
  * Quantization fallback: requests routed to quantized variant will be marked and excluded from SLO counts (we'll include them in a separate degraded-metrics report).
- Rollback/credit criteria:
  * Soft alert: if >3% of 15-min windows breach p95 in the 14-day window, we will convene a joint ops review.
  * Hard review/rollback: if >7% of windows breach p95 for >6 hours cumulative, Redwood reserves the right to pause the rollout and revert traffic to the pre-rollout configuration until remediation. No automatic credits during the 14-day carveout; post-carveout credits subject to contract language.
- Evidence: daily report, sampled traces (linkable), and completed slo-evidence-template.xlsx.
- Next steps:
  1) Please confirm you can add X-AH-Canary header to pilot traffic (or provide an alternate filter).
  2) If agreed, sign the attached DocuSign amendment (link) to add the 14-day probationary carveout and measurement language to the SOW.

I'll attach Karthik's CI numbers when they arrive; we expect the 0.5% sample to produce stable p95 estimates for their volume.

If you prefer tighter p95 bounds we can discuss dedicated capacity (Dedicated pool) as an option.

Thanks — looking forward to getting AstraHealth live.

—Monica Patel
